text:
Alex: Heads up — after the runtime deploy we pushed last night I'm seeing p95 generation latency climb ~20% on mixed initgen traffic. Sampled traces point to longer handshake waits in the prefill queue. infra-bot: deploy info below.

infra-bot: Deploy: runtime/2026.03.17.22 - rollout to canary - image sha256:abcd1234 - changelist: phase-split scheduling tweaks

Rachel: cc @Sam @Jorge — this sounds like the phase-aware scheduling patch we merged?

Sam: Yup, I shipped the prefill/decode gating change around 22:01. I also adjusted token_budget_target for mixed flows. Looking into the traces now.

Alex: Quick profiling snapshot: top of trace shows stall at KVWarmupTask waiting on prefill fence. Key metric: `wait_for_prefill_ms` went from ~45ms -> ~120ms in canary. Decode tokens per batch also dropped.

Jorge: That pattern smells like KV priming order flip. If prefill batches are getting deprioritized, decode may miss hot KV and fall back to coldpath kernels more often.

Sam: Running a microbench with `--profiling=handshake` on canary. Early numbers: prefill batch size median down 32 -> 18 under same load, token_budget_utilization lower.

Rachel: Did we change batch formation heuristics or queue policy besides the phase gating? I thought only kernel affinity was tweaked.

Sam: I changed token_budget_target to 60% for mixed flows to reduce tail latency for small requests. In hindsight that might be starving prefill batch formation and reducing KV priming effectiveness.

Alex: Repro steps I used: `stress_mixed.py --seq=2048 --rps=120 --canary`. Compare `kv_miss_rate` and `kernel_switch_count`. Observed kv_miss_rate up 0.08 -> 0.21 and kernel_switch +40%.

perf-bot: Alert: p95_generation_latency increased 19% on canary (runtime/2026.03.17.22). Metrics: tokens/s -3.2%, kv_miss +160%, kernel_switch +42%.

Sam: Ok I'm reverting the token_budget_target tweak on canary now and re-running the microbench. Also adding a minimal harness that isolates prefill vs decode thresholds.

Rachel: Alternative idea: make kernel selection biased towards a 'kv-primed' kernel for the first N batches of a session until kv-hit stabilizes. Might avoid coldpath thrash without increasing batch caps.

Jorge: Technically doable: introduce a short-lived `kv-prime-bias` flag that prefers kernel A for initial batches. Need to simulate throughput impact — don't want to degrade overall tokens/sec.

Alex: For immediate mitigation, revert heuristics and collect flamegraphs + full traces. Sam, can you post flamegraphs and a small test harness link?

Sam: Reverted and running. Quick flame summary: decode time/token jumped +12% in decode stage; prefill queue wait increased +70ms. Uploaded trace: /internal/perf/3845554321/trace.html

Rachel: Good. Next steps checklist I'll create: 1) instrument `session_kv_hit_after_n_batches`, 2) A/B test `kv-prime-bias` vs reverted heuristics, 3) run simulation sweep across token_budget_target {50,60,70,80} with mixed and pure decode workloads.

Alex: If we can reproduce reliably in microbench, we can try kernel-selection fallback that detects high kv_miss and forces priming kernel until hit rate recovers. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
